claim.claim-text: a first wing (110) section of the telescoping wing (110) system; and a second wing (110) section comprising a substantially hollow interior configured to stow the first wing (110) section, wherein the first wing (110) section and the second wing (110) section form a first wingspan in a first arrangement, the first arrangement comprising the first wing (110) section stowed within the interior of the second wing (110) section, and wherein the first wing (110) section and the second wing (110) section form a second wingspan in a second arrangement, the second arrangement comprising the second wing (110) section displaced along at least a portion of a length between a first end and a second end of the first wing (110) section.
2. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 1, wherein the first wing (110) section is attached to a fuselage (106) of an aerial vehicle.

3. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 2, wherein at least a portion of the first wingspan and the second wingspan of the aerial vehicle is comprised of approximately a length of the second wing (110) section and a length of an exposed portion of the first wing (110) section.

4. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 2, wherein the length of the exposed portion of the first wing (110) section increases as the second wing (110) section is displaced by at least a portion of the length between the first end and the second end of the first wing (110) section in the second arrangement

5. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 4, wherein the displacement of the second wing (110) section along the length of the first wing (110) section extends the first wingspan of the aerial vehicle by approximately the displacement length to form the second wingspan.
6. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 1, further comprising an actuator configured to drive the displacement of the second wing (110) section.

7. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 1, wherein the first wing (110) section and the second wing (110) section are configured, in the first arrangement, to be stowed against the fuselage (106) of the aerial vehicle.

8. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 7, wherein the first wing (110) section and the second wing (110) section are configured, in the first arrangement, to be deployed at an angle relative to the fuselage (106) of the aerial vehicle.

9. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 8, wherein the first wing (110) section and the second wing (110) section are configured to transition from the first arrangement to the second arrangement at the deployed angle.
11. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 10, wherein the interior of the outer section (310) is not obstructed by the control surface.

12. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 10, wherein the control surface is configured to attach to the trailing-edge of the outer section (310), via the externally mounted hinge (1215), so as to maximize the interior volume of the outer section (310).

13. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 10, wherein the attachment of the control surface along the trailing-edge of the external surface of the outer section (310) enables the inner section (305), when stowed in the first configuration, to overlap at least a portion of a length of the trailing-edge control surface attachment

14. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 11, wherein the telescoping means is enabled to provide an improved wingspan ratio between the first configuration and the second configuration due to, at least in part, the inner section (305) being configurable within the interior of the outer section (310) without obstruction from the control surface attachment.

15. The telescoping wing (110) system of claim 11, wherein a surface area ratio between the inner section (305) and outer section (310) is increased due to, at least in part, the inner section (305) being configurable within the interior of the outer section (310) without obstruction from the control surface attachment.
